A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sinusoidal initialization work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D are readable and support comparison. The explicitly unfinished ViT reporting in v1 can be matched to its completion in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original training results across vision and language models, activation-skewness measurements, and synthetic and randomized-arcsine analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, completes the ViT comparison, and adds activation-function and initialization comparisons.

M1.justification: Equation (1), sinusoidal frequencies and phases, Glorot variance scaling, and zero-bias initialization remain unchanged. The new m < n restriction qualifies a theorem rather than changing the initialization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, ImageNet-1k, WikiText2 masked language modeling, and synthetic Normal/Uniform inputs. The added experiments reuse existing datasets and tasks; they change comparators or model configurations.

E2.justification: Appendix D.2 introduces direct comparisons against Zhao et al.'s Zero initialization and Blumenfeld et al.'s method, adding previously absent deterministic competitors. Appendix D.1 also adds randomized-arcsine initialization to a training comparison, beyond its existing activation diagnostics. These additions concern ResNet-50/CIFAR-100 with SGD; Table 3 retains its original comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 4 adds a MobileNetV3 control replacing HardSwish with ReLU. The retained benchmarks' metrics, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes, and epoch budgets remain unchanged. The new early-stopping and equal-duration explanation documents the existing evaluation rather than establishing that its protocol changed.

E4.justification: v3 adds the MobileNetV3 activation-function check and extends the randomized-arcsine analysis from activation imbalance to training convergence in Figure 9. These are targeted additions to the existing mechanism analyses; the earlier depth, input-distribution, and activation diagnostics remain.

E5.justification: Both versions' Appendix C reports three repetitions, mean results, and computed but omitted standard deviations. v3 adds no confidence intervals, significance tests, seed details, or changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises ViT maximum accuracy for Orthogonal/LSUV from 28.1/29.2 to 28.2/29.6 and fills their missing AUC values with 25/24. Reported average accuracy advantages over Default/Orthogonal/LSUV change from 4.8/2.0/4.1% to 4.9/1.7/3.4%; AUC advantages over Orthogonal/LSUV change from 6.1/19.2% to 5.7/18.0%. New appendix curves and the qualitative MobileNetV3-ReLU finding add localized results; most existing results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds Theorem 2 on asymptotic skewness under random initialization for thresholds tending to zero, with an accompanying Appendix B.1 proof. It also restricts the old row-cancellation theorem, now Theorem 3, to m < n and explicitly establishes the nonzero geometric-series denominator. The existing general threshold-equivalence theorem is retained and renumbered.

C1.justification: The three principal contributions remain deterministic sinusoidal initialization, an activation-skewness framework, and improved training performance. The novelty framing now acknowledges an already explored deterministic direction, and the abstract and conclusion revise the headline average accuracy advantage from 4.8% to 4.9%.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly attributes MobileNetV3's exception to an interaction between HardSwish and initialization, citing the ReLU replacement experiment. Section 3.2 explicitly frames the analysis around ReLU-like activations, and Appendix D.2 acknowledges that the deterministic comparison covers only one setup. Appendix A's principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The generic GitHub placeholder becomes a specific Sinusoidal-Initialization repository address, also provided on the first page. Section 4 newly explains early stopping and equal training durations for AUC comparisons. Existing implementation descriptions, hyperparameter tables, hardware, and runtime information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds and discusses Blumenfeld et al. (2020) and Zhao et al. (2022) as prior deterministic approaches. This substantively recasts the research gap from deterministic preservation of initialization statistics to demonstrated accuracy and convergence advantages over random initialization, correcting the earlier largely unexplored-direction positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose and the overall section structure are retained. Local changes include expanded explanations, a positional-encoding footnote, updated author affiliation and conference text, and insertion of Appendix D.2 before the existing training-plots subsection. v3 also introduces malformed activation-name text and repeats a sentence in the MobileNet discussion.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 9 and 10, completes the ViT comparator curves in Figure 6, and clarifies Table 3's caption. Tables and figures are locally repositioned, while the former Figure 9 is retained as Figure 11. The overall visual style and other displays remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves completeness and reproducibility information by finishing the ViT comparison, supplying a specific code address, acknowledging and testing deterministic alternatives, and correcting the row-cancellation assumption. The gains are limited by weaknesses in the added evidence: the MobileNet-ReLU result lacks numerical detail, and Figures 9–10 show Sinusoidal accuracy near 39%, versus Table 3's 51.9% for the stated ResNet-50/CIFAR-100/SGD setup, without explaining the discrepancy.
